origins.section: A Run Is Repeatable When Its Plan Digest Repeats
A Golden Plan Catches a Regression the Rule Tests Miss
A Warm Start Changed the Search, Not the Time, on These Runs

gates.says: all 3 of this quiz's answerable readings held and each was taken over the question as it stands

recorded.prompt:q-harness: Read the whole lesson page, then this question. Using only what the page states, which option does the page decide is correct? Quote or cite the deciding passage.
recorded.outcome:q-harness: Three identical digests show that this export, with this OR-Tools version and one HiGHS thread, gives the same plan.
recorded.prompt:q-golden: Read the whole lesson page, then this question. Using only what the page states, which option does the page decide is correct? Quote or cite the deciding passage.
recorded.outcome:q-golden: golden check, window cut one year short: ['P001: start 2029 -> None', 'npv 2,473 -> 1,396'] / "Only a comparison with a known plan sees that P001 vanished"
recorded.prompt:q-warm: Read the whole lesson page, then this question. Using only what the page states, which option does the page decide is correct? Quote or cite the deciding passage.
recorded.outcome:q-warm: The warm run did exactly the same work as the cold one, to the node: on this run the infeasible start changed nothing.

recorded.prompt:q-harness: Answer ONLY from this question's own text: its stem and its options. Use no knowledge of the subject at all; treat every term as a word you have never met. Pick an option only when the wording itself singles it out: it is longer or more specific than the others, it repeats words from the stem, the others carry absolute terms such as 'always' or 'never', the stem's grammar fits it alone, or it restates the stem. A cue decides only when it clearly singles out one option over every other; a weak cue, or one another option shares, decides nothing. Otherwise answer 'none'. Say which cue decided it, or that none did.
